newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson says investors back proposal in takeover war.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson says investors back proposal in takeover war.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co., the hostile bidder for Great Western Financial Corp., said Friday it won investor support on a proposal urging the California savings and loan to open negotiations with its rival.
Great Western, which has spurned Ahmanson's bid and signed a definitive merger agreement March 6 with Seattle-based savings and loan Washington Mutual Inc., said Ahmanson's claim was premature.
But analysts saw Ahmanson's announcement as a victory.

"I believe it should be construed as a victory. If Great Western chooses to ignore the consent solicitation, they may face shareholder action," said Thomas Theurkauf, analyst with Keefe Bruyette Woods.
Smith Barney brokerage analyst Thomas O'Donnell said he believes a good assessment of shareholders' sentiment is the spread between the two offers.

Irwindale, Calif.-based Ahmanson's proposal to exchange up to 1.2 shares of Ahmanson stock for each share of Great Western was valued at about $42.30 a share, or $5.9 billion, Friday. Washington Mutual's offer to exchange 0.9 of its shares for each Great Western share, was valued at about $40.95 a share, or $5.7 billion.

Ahmanson stock dropped $2 to $35.25 Friday, while Great Western fell $2 to $39.75, both in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Washington Mutual also fell, dropping $2.25 to $45.50 on Nasdaq.
Chatsworth, Calif.-based Great Western said its response to Ahmanson's consent solicitation would come in a week or so when the votes are counted and certified by an independent firm.

On Wednesday, Ahmanson -- parent of Home Savings of America, the country's largest savings institution -- said a majority of the shares voted in the consent solicitation backed three other proposals, including one that would require Great Western to hold its annual meeting by May 6.

But Great Western said Friday it had slated the meeting for June 13. Ahmanson responded by amending a Delaware lawsuit to allege that holding the meeting in June would represent a breach of duty by Great Western.
Ahmanson is seeking to have three independent directors voted to the Great Western board at the annual meeting.
O'Donnell said Ahmanson's better-than-expected first-quarter earnings released earlier this week and the preliminary results of the consent solicitation have breathed new life into its bid.

"Ahmanson's offer to acquire Great Western, which looked like it was very much a long shot late last week and earlier this week, has sprung back to life," he said, noting that the Ahmanson offer actually began the week with a negative premium.
Washington Mutual is the No. 3 thrift in the country.
